chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There was a woman called Umm Tayba who used to perform circumcision on girls. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called her and said to her: 'O Umm Tayba! When you circumcise a woman, make a snip and do not scrape excessively, for it is clearer for the complexion and more pleasurable for the husband.'

key_terms.تَخْفِضُ: To circumcise (specifically females, by removing the clitoris or prepuce)
key_terms.وَلَا تُجْحِفِي: And do not scrape/excise excessively (removing more than necessary)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method and extent of female circumcision according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophetic tradition of female circumcision (khitan al-jawari) through Umm Tayba, emphasizing a moderate, non-exhaustive approach ('ashimmi' rather than 'tujhifi') to preserve physical beauty and enhance marital intimacy. In Shia scholarship, this is often cited to support the permissibility of the practice while cautioning against excessive removal of tissue, aligning with the principle of avoiding harm (darar). The instruction reflects a balance between ritual purification and practical well-being, rooted in the specific context of the early Muslim community.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from Amro Bin Sabit, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘There used to be a woman call Umm Tayba who used to cut (the genitals) of the girls. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> called her over, so he<sup>saww</sup> said to her: ‘O Umm Tayba! Whenever you cut the (genitals of) the girls, so (only a) snip and do not scrape away, for it is clearer for the colour and more pleasurable in the presence of the husband’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Khalaf ibn Hammad from ‘Amr ibn Thabit who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that there was a woman called ‘Umm Taybah and she lowered girls. The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, called her and said, ‘O ’Umm Taybah, when you lower a woman make it (as little as) a scratch but do not be excessive. It clears the color and is more enjoyable to the husband.’”
